summaryBox.title: Transition Elements Taxonomy
summaryBox.takeaway: Transition elements have incomplete d^(1-9) subshells. Group 12 (Zn, Cd, Hg) are non-transition / pseudo-transition elements (d¹⁰ in ground & all ionic states).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
d-BLOCK TAXONOMY & EXCLUSIONS
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                                                   ▼
  TRUE TRANSITION ELEMENTS                                 PSEUDO-TRANSITION ELEMENTS
  Possess incomplete $(n-1)d^{1-9}$ subshells.            Group 12 ($\text{Zn, Cd, Hg}$): Possess completely
  ├── $3d$ Series: $\text{Sc } (Z=21) \rightarrow \text{Cu } (Z=29)$  filled $d^{10}$ subshells in ground state AND
  └── Displays variable OS, color, & magnetism             all oxidation states ($\text{Zn}^{2+}: 3d^{10}$).
conceptBreakdown.content:
The d-Block Elements occupy Groups 3 to 12 of the periodic table, where $(n-1)d$ subshells are progressively filled. A Transition Element is defined as an element possessing partially filled d-orbitals in its neutral ground-state atom or in any of its common oxidation states.

- **General Outer Electronic Configuration**:
$$\mathbf{(n-1)d^{1-10} \, ns^{1-2}}$$

- **Ground-State Anomalies in 3d Series**:
  - **Chromium ($\text{Cr}, Z=24$)**: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$ (Half-filled $3d^5$ subshell stability)
  - **Copper ($\text{Cu}, Z=29$)**: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^1$ (Fully-filled $3d^{10}$ subshell stability)

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 Enthalpy of Atomization (Δ_a H°) & Metallic Bonding
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Enthalpy of Atomization (Δ_a H°) & Metallic Bonding
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
$3d$ SERIES ENTHALPY OF ATOMIZATION TREND
                    
   $\Delta_a H^\circ$ (kJ/mol) ▲
                    │         /\
                    │        /  \     /\
                    │  Sc───/    \───/  \
                    │      V     Cr  Fe  \
                    │                     \─── Cu ─── Zn (Lowest $\Delta_a H^\circ$)
                    │             Mn (ANOMALOUS DIP!)
                    └───────────────────────────────────► $3d$ Element ($Z$)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Transition metals possess high melting points, boiling points, and high Enthalpies of Atomization ($\Delta_a H^\circ$) due to strong metallic bonding resulting from overlapping $ns$ electrons combined with covalent bonding from unpaired $(n-1)d$ electrons.

- **The Manganese Anomaly ($\text{Mn}, Z=25$)**: Manganese ($3d^5 4s^2$) possesses 5 unpaired d-electrons, yet exhibits an unusually low melting point and low $\Delta_a H^\circ$ ($281\text{ kJ/mol}$).
  - **Cause**: The stable half-filled $3d^5$ configuration holds its d-electrons tightly localized around individual nuclei, minimizing d-d inter-atomic orbital overlap and reducing covalent character in the metallic lattice.
- **Group 12 Minimal $\Delta_a H^\circ$**: Zinc ($\text{Zn}, 126\text{ kJ/mol}$) has no unpaired d-electrons ($3d^{10} 4s^2$); bonding is mediated purely by weak $4s$ electrons.

quickRevision: Zn, Cd, Hg are pseudo-transition metals (d¹⁰ in all states).
Manganese has an anomalously low Δ_a H° (281 kJ/mol) due to tightly localized 3d⁵ electrons.
Zinc has the lowest Δ_a H° (126 kJ/mol) due to 0 unpaired d-electrons.
